title: Quenched Flaky Korean Zucchini Namul
description: A low-carb, umami-rich Korean dish featuring zucchini and nuka-pickle, perfect for a crowd, this quenched flaky namul is a delicious and healthy side dish.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together sesame oil, soy sauce, garlic, and ginger to make the dressing.
Add the diced zucchini to the bowl and toss to coat with the dressing.
Let the zucchini sit for 10 minutes to allow it to release its moisture.
After 10 minutes, squeeze out as much liquid from the zucchini as possible using a clean kitchen towel or cheesecloth.
In a pan, heat the nuka-pickle over medium heat until it is lightly browned and fragrant.
Add the squeezed zucchini to the pan and stir to combine with the nuka-pickle.
Cook for an additional 2 minutes, stirring frequently, until the zucchini is lightly browned and crispy.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the toasted sesame seeds, salt, and black pepper.
Add the water to the pan and stir to combine, allowing the namul to quenched and flaky.
Serve the quenched flaky Korean zucchini namul hot, garnished with additional toasted sesame seeds if desired.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
